title: Beatrix and the Regiment
premise: In 1847 Vienna, Felix Halloran—a young woman living as a male clockmaker's apprentice to escape her family's ruin—summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, finds an abandoned child at its door with a note ordering her to forget the face. The child is tied to a murdered witness in a corruption case against the Imperial Treasury, and the men who silenced him are closing in on anyone who might remember. As Felix repairs the clock by day and hides the child by night, she gathers a found family of workshop outcasts who help her preserve the testimony the dead man hid inside the clock itself. The story ends with Felix testifying under her true name at great personal cost, the conspirators exposed, and the child adopted into the workshop family—justice won not by the law's speed but by memory kept alive.
about_author: Quentin Reyes is a former museum conservator of scientific instruments who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century clocks before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about ordinary people who keep time—and secrets—for a living.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Felix Halloran, five years hidden in Herr Brandt's workshop as a boy apprentice, receives the observatory commission that could secure her future. POV Felix. Beat: cautious hope shadowed by the fear that visibility means danger.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to the night Felix fled her family's bankruptcy and took her dead brother's name; Brandt suspected and said nothing. POV Felix. Beat: grief braided with gratitude for chosen silence.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Arriving at the observatory at dawn, Felix finds a girl of six abandoned on the steps with a note: forget this face. Inside, the master clock has been sabotaged, not merely broken. POV Felix. Beat: dread—the sabotage was meant to destroy something.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix discovers a hidden compartment in the escapement containing coded papers signed by a treasury clerk, Anton Voss, whose murder the papers gossip about. POV Felix. Beat: the weight of evidence no one asked her to carry.

chapters.title: Herr Brandt's Warning
chapters.summary: Brandt recognizes the seal on the papers and orders Felix to burn them; his own brother died after touching treasury business. POV Brandt. Beat: fear disguised as pragmatism, love disguised as anger.

chapters.title: A Name for the Girl
chapters.summary: Unable to abandon the child, Felix smuggles her into the workshop loft; the seamstress Marta and the deaf engraver Ivo quietly conspire to hide her. POV Felix. Beat: the first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: Men Who Ask About Clocks
chapters.summary: A well-dressed inspector, Kessler, visits asking about the observatory repair and about 'a clerk's effects.' Felix lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. POV Felix. Beat: the hunter glimpsed through civility.

chapters.title: Decoding Voss
chapters.summary: Ivo's engraving eye cracks the cipher: ledgers proving Kessler's patron, Director Albrecht, laundered seized estates—and Voss hid the originals in the clock. POV Ivo. Beat: quiet triumph curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Marta's Needle
chapters.summary: Marta recalls dressing Voss's widow and realizes the 'forget this face' note is in Albrecht's hand—the child is Voss's daughter, left where only a clockmaker would look. POV Marta. Beat: memory as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Clock Stops
chapters.summary: Kessler returns and demands the master clock be declared unrepairable; Felix stalls by day while working by candlelight, knowing the finished clock will expose the hiding place. POV Felix. Beat: racing against both mechanism and men.

chapters.title: Fire in the Lane
chapters.summary: A suspicious fire guts a neighboring shop; Brandt understands it is a message. He stops resisting and gives Felix his brother's old contacts among honest magistrates. POV Brandt. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Child Speaks
chapters.summary: The girl, Lena, finally speaks, repeating phrases her father drilled into her—a verbal key confirming the cipher's final page. POV Lena. Beat: innocence carrying unbearable inheritance.

chapters.title: Albrecht's Offer
chapters.summary: Director Albrecht summons Felix personally, offering money, legitimacy, even papers making her apprenticeship legal under her own name—if the clock is delivered empty. POV Felix. Beat: temptation aimed precisely at her oldest wound.

chapters.title: Five Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Felix nearly accepts; Marta confronts her: invisibility protected Felix, never Lena. Felix chooses, at last, to be seen. POV Felix. Beat: the novel's moral hinge.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Ivo engraves duplicate plates; Marta sews the ledger pages into a christening gown; three hiding places become one plan. POV ensemble via Ivo. Beat: found family functioning as an instrument.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Workshop
chapters.summary: A journeyman, bribed, tips off Kessler; soldiers raid the loft and find it empty—but they take Brandt for questioning. POV Felix. Beat: guilt, fury, and the cost of staying.

chapters.title: The Observatory at Midnight
chapters.summary: Felix completes the master clock and sets Voss's original plates inside its striking train, timed to open publicly during the equinox demonstration. POV Felix. Beat: craftsmanship as testimony.

chapters.title: What Kessler Knows
chapters.summary: Kessler, himself compromised, offers Felix a deal: Brandt's release for the plates. She negotiates hard, learning he fears Albrecht more than the law. POV Kessler. Beat: enemy revealed as another trapped man.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: At the public demonstration, dignitaries watch the restored clock strike; the compartment opens before the crowd, exposing the plates. Albrecht moves to seize them—but Magistrate Ehrlich, Brandt's contact, is waiting. POV Felix. Beat: climax—memory made public, irreversible.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: To authenticate the ledger, Felix must testify as Beatrix Halloran, revealing her disguise; she does so, voice steady, holding Lena's hand. POV Beatrix. Beat: identity reclaimed at maximum cost.

chapters.title: After the Striking
chapters.summary: Albrecht arrested; Kessler turns crown's evidence; Brandt released and formally takes Beatrix as partner, not apprentice. POV Brandt. Beat: debts acknowledged, silence ended.

chapters.title: The Clock Still Runs
chapters.summary: One year later: the workshop thrives, Lena learns the trade, and Beatrix winds the observatory clock each equinox, remembering aloud so nothing is forgotten again. POV Beatrix. Beat: resolution—justice outside the law became justice within it, carried by those who refused to forget.
